title: Normalized coefficient evaluation of the clopen section factor
statement: Use a proper/open commutative square k:V->W, r:V->S, p:W->T, i:S->T, with k,i quasi-compact open and r,p proper, and arbitrary inverse coefficient rings R_n. Put q=pr_S and b=pr_W on W times_T S. Define sectionArrow and strictSectionArrow as in [def-sp-varying-ring-clopen-arrow-factors]. Fix n. There is one natural transformation c from D(q^*) D(b_!) to D(r^*) D(k_!) in the ordinary single-coefficient R_n derived categories with the following properties. For all N in D(system_S), ev_W(sectionArrow_N);evalJ_k(G_r N);J_k(evalG_r(N)) = evalJ_b(G_q N);J_b(evalG_q(N));c(ev_S N). For all N in D(strict towers over R_n), the identical equation holds for strictSectionArrow, strict evaluation at zero, and strict evalJ and evalG. The constructed clopen projector and outgoing composition identifications alone enter these equations; no cartesian beta factor is included.

proof.text: The geometric lift s=(k,r):V->W times_T S is open and closed by proper-over-separated and the factorization of the open map k. Cover the fibre product by its image and complementary open. On the image, restriction of the ordinary modulePi is the open-unit identification, by the triangle equation for pull/direct image and the definition of moduleOpenToP. On the complement its target vanishes, since extension by zero has no sections supported there. These restrictions determine the module-sheaf map by the clopen product decomposition.

proof.text: Coefficient evaluation commutes with restrictions and extension by zero and preserves the normalized open unit. The evaluated modulePi is consequently identity on the same image and zero on the same complement. The strict termwise projector has precisely these two restrictions. Thus both are the same single-coefficient projector; the argument applies degreewise to complexes without detecting arbitrary derived morphisms by their evaluations.

proof.text: Compose the single-coefficient projection, after q^*, with b_! and the outgoing identifications bs=k and qs=r, to construct c. Pullback composition is preserved because its direct-image mate restricts sections along the same pullback-pasting map. Open composition is its open-adjoint conjugate; equality transports are proof-irrelevant. Substitute these equations into moduleSectionArrow and apply exact localization. Strict derived pi is the same localized ordinary projection: exact localization preserves the units and the inverse open-to-direct comparison on the clopen immersion. Localization factor isomorphisms and essential surjectivity give the displayed equations at every derived input.

lean.statement:
theorem clopenSectionEvaluation {V W S T : Scheme.{u}} (k : V ⟶ W) (r : V ⟶ S)
    (p : W ⟶ T) (i : S ⟶ T) [IsOpenImmersion k] [IsOpenImmersion i]
    [QuasiCompact k] [QuasiCompact i] [IsProper r] [IsProper p]
    (h : k ≫ p = r ≫ i) (n : ℕ) :
    ∃ a : (StrictTower.modulePullback (R n) (pullback.snd p i)).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
          (StrictTower.moduleJ (R n) (pullback.fst p i)).mapDerivedCategory ⟶
        (StrictTower.modulePullback (R n) r).mapDerivedCategory ⋙
          (StrictTower.moduleJ (R n) k).mapDerivedCategory,
      (∀ N : Derived R φ S,
        (ev R φ W n).map ((sectionArrow R φ k r p i h).app N) ≫
            (evalJ R φ k n).hom.app ((G R φ r).obj N) ≫
            (StrictTower.moduleJ (R n) k).mapDerivedCategory.map
              ((evalG R φ r n).hom.app N) =
          (evalJ R φ (pullback.fst p i) n).hom.app
              ((G R φ (pullback.snd p i)).obj N) ≫
            (StrictTower.moduleJ (R n) (pullback.fst p i)).mapDerivedCategory.map
              ((evalG R φ (pullback.snd p i) n).hom.app N) ≫ a.app ((ev R φ S n).obj N)) ∧
      (∀ N : StrictTower.Derived (R n) S,
        (StrictTower.ev (R n) W 0).map ((strictSectionArrow (R n) k r p i h).app N) ≫
            (StrictTower.evalJ (R n) k 0).hom.app ((StrictTower.G (R n) r).obj N) ≫
            (StrictTower.moduleJ (R n) k).mapDerivedCategory.map
              ((StrictTower.evalG (R n) r 0).hom.app N) =
          (StrictTower.evalJ (R n) (pullback.fst p i) 0).hom.app
              ((StrictTower.G (R n) (pullback.snd p i)).obj N) ≫
            (StrictTower.moduleJ (R n) (pullback.fst p i)).mapDerivedCategory.map
              ((StrictTower.evalG (R n) (pullback.snd p i) 0).hom.app N) ≫
            a.app ((StrictTower.ev (R n) S 0).obj N))
